clue.text: Give birth, with assistance

parts.note: assistance means help

explanation.surface: A midwife's role: helping at a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a dog or other animal, to bring forth young is to whelp.

clue.text: Merry-maker is a wife-beater

parts.note: a beater is one who attacks, an assailer

explanation.surface: A grim reveller who turns out to be a domestic abuser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a' only links; the wife-beater is read as W followed by a word for an attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassailer is a reveller who drinks toasts and goes carousing, especially at Christmas.

clue.text: Girl for whom I care madly

indicators.note: madly signals that the letters of the two words are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A lovestruck admission about the girl one cares for passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name.

clue.text: Unreasonable, like Animal Farm?

explanation.surface: A complaint that Orwell's farm is run irrationally.
explanation.walkthrough: In Orwell's novel Animal Farm the farm is led by pigs, so it is literally headed by pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and stupidly stubborn people are called this; and the farm in Orwell's fable has swine at its head.

clue.text: Run out of plump fish? Get producing

parts.note: plump means fat

indicators.note: out of tells us the letter for run is removed from the combined words

parts.note: a herring is a fish
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A recipe asks you to stop using fat fish and start making something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is the old verb beget: to sire offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire children is to beget them, the old sense of get.

clue.text: Butter up, but not so much up

explanation.surface: Advice on praising someone, but less lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise insincerely is to flatter; something less raised or more level is flatter.

clue.text: Get up and steal away

explanation.surface: Someone rises from bed and sneaks off quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's departure into the air is its rising off the ground; to leave suddenly and quietly is to depart in that phrase.

clue.text: Aim to improve husband for woman

parts.note: to edit a text is to work to make it better

explanation.surface: A wife's plan to make her husband a better man.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a female first name.

clue.text: In the absence of a man, boy was brought up shy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: absence of means the word for a man is missing from the word before it

parts.note: the gives its own letters before the deletion
he is a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Trevor is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy raised without a father figure grew up timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absence of a man' takes HE from THE, leaving T; 'was brought up' reverses TREVOR to ROVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a reserved, inward-looking person, a timid or retiring type.

clue.text: Eat too much Cheddar?

explanation.surface: A warning against overindulging in cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar Gorge is a famous ravine in Somerset, England, as well as the village that names the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to overeat; Cheddar in Somerset has a famous limestone ravine.

clue.text: Shoe cast by champion

parts.note: to cast is to throw or sling
to champion a cause is to support or back it

explanation.surface: A shoe flung by a sporting champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A slingback is a woman's shoe held on by a strap behind the heel.

clue.text: Put in the ground after start of cold weather

indicators.note: after start of says we keep what follows once the opening letter is removed

parts.note: winter is the season of cold weather

explanation.surface: Planting or burial delayed until the first frost.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, especially a corpse.

clue.text: A foundation must be lower

parts.note: a base is a foundation

explanation.surface: A builder's rule that footings must sit deeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase is to humiliate or degrade, bringing someone down in dignity.

clue.text: Shoot-out in book is not unsavoury

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled letters go inside the book

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A review saying a novel with a gunfight is quite palatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot-out' looks like one noun but splits: 'out' is the anagram signal working on the first half alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is tasty and appetising, the litotes 'not unsavoury'.

clue.text: Give respectability to Scottish entertainer not at first accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the first letter is taken inside the entertainer's name

parts.note: Sir Harry Lauder was a famous Scottish music-hall singer

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word not

explanation.surface: A Scottish performer is made respectable despite an initial snub.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Lauder was a Scottish music-hall star of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass dirty money through legitimate channels is to make it look respectable, as with washing.

clue.text: Tidy, but no class is silent

indicators.note: no means the letters for class are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: a tidy room is uncluttered
CL is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A neat but low-born person keeps quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Words never spoken are unvoiced, left unsaid.

clue.text: Flap on dress providing modest concealment

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the flap after the dress

parts.note: fig is dress, as in the phrase in full fig
a leaf is a hinged flap, as of a table

explanation.surface: A dress with a flap that keeps the wearer decent.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical statues cover nudity with this foliage, so it stands for any coy covering.

clue.text: Unnecessary former utility room

parts.note: gash is British slang for spare or surplus
former means older, earlier

explanation.surface: A redundant old laundry room in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utility room' is not the household laundry room but storage space for a gas utility's supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is the large tank where a gas company stores its supply, a store-room for a public utility.

clue.text: Department of State about to recognise portent

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department
re means about, concerning
taken as written
ken is to know or recognise, chiefly in Scots

explanation.surface: A government department is about to spot an omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' is two pieces, not a phrase: RE then TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretoken is a sign or omen of something to come.

clue.text: OUP collection

parts.note: a round letter O placed above UP gives these three letters

explanation.surface: Oxford University Press brings out an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: OUP is Oxford University Press, but here it is O (round) and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of news items or cattle is a summary gathering, a compilation.

clue.text: Supply evidence nothing's missing — a turn-up for the judge

indicators.note: missing means the letter for nothing is dropped from the evidence word

parts.note: proof is evidence
O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: a turn-up in a down clue means the referee is read upwards

parts.note: a referee, or ref, is a judge in sport

explanation.surface: A lawyer produces evidence with nothing missing, a surprise for the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops O from PROOF; 'a turn-up' reverses REF to FER.
explanation.definitionFit: To proffer is to offer or hold out for acceptance.

clue.text: Maybe an inspector that calls?

parts.note: plays on Priestley's play An Inspector Calls: an inspector who calls is one example of someone who drops in

explanation.surface: A nod to J. B. Priestley's play about a policeman's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: An Inspector Calls is a well-known play by J. B. Priestley.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller who comes to see you, an inspector among them, is a guest at your door.

clue.text: Starts of sessions postponed: takes a turn outside for an hour

indicators.note: outside means the turning word goes round the opening letters

parts.note: to veer is to turn or change direction

indicators.note: starts of picks the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Delayed sessions, and someone strolls out for an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hour' is a canonical hour of church prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is one of the canonical hours of daily prayer, the evening office.

clue.text: Explain vote?

explanation.surface: A request to account for how someone balloted.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an idea understood is to communicate it; one marks a ballot paper with an X.

clue.text: A birdie — beat that

parts.note: to pip is to beat narrowly
it can stand for that, as a pronoun

explanation.surface: A golfer scores one under par and challenges a rival to better it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birdie' looks like golf but is just a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small songbird of open country.

clue.text: One that's discreet about one's supposed right

indicators.note: about means the discreet creature goes around the numeral

parts.note: a clam is a secretive person, who clams up
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A discreet person speaking about what they believe is their entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim is an assertion of entitlement that may or may not be upheld.

clue.text: Complete circuit, or just part

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A choice between a whole lap or only a portion of one.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a full revolution of one body around another.

clue.text: Memorial tablet for the high-ranking?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plaque is reserved for top officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Church memorial plaques are engraved metal plates; senior officers are known collectively as top metal of that kind.

clue.text: Vessel protected by annual coating

indicators.note: protected by means the vessel sits inside the letters for annual

parts.note: PA is per annum, yearly
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat shielded by a yearly lick of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' means a coat, a garment, not a layer of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak with a hood is a kind of warm outer garment.

clue.text: Major position, for example, Irish composer finds disagreeable

parts.note: John Field was an Irish composer, inventor of the nocturne
rank means foul, offensive

explanation.surface: A music critic dislikes an Irish composer's best-known piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' is the army rank, not a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is a commissioned officer above captain, in the grade between company and general officers.

clue.text: Boundaries of the Wash?

parts.note: the Wash is a broad bay in eastern England, but a wash is also a bath, whose grimy rings show where the water reached

explanation.surface: Asks where the Wash, an English bay, begins and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large estuary on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines left by high water on a shore, or rings of dirt round a bath, show where the water came up to.

clue.text: Dares infantry to obscure sappers' objective

indicators.note: to obscure says the answer lies concealed within the next words

explanation.surface: A general dares his foot soldiers to cover the engineers' target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sappers' looks like military engineers but means those who tap trees for sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tappers of trees collect gum, the sticky exudate, from pines.
